Behaviors of Individuals
and Groups Lab

Social psychologyUnderstanding the individual
SociologyUnderstanding the group
Network scienceUnderstanding the connections

People don’t
change alone.

Our lives are connected in ways that are easy to miss — and essential to understand.

BIG Lab brings social psychology, sociology and network science together. We investigate how attitudes and behaviours form, how they change through experience, and how those changes spread through relationships.

How does change
find its way?

Five connected research areas. One shared interest in the forces that shape individuals, relationships and groups.

Read our publications
Development and spread of attitudes and behaviours

We examine how attitudes and behaviours emerge and evolve, and how individual changes travel through relationships, groups and society.

Related projects
Social influence

How do other people shape what we believe and do? We study interpersonal influence through experiments and longitudinal social network analysis.

Related publications
Intra- and intergroup dynamics

We explore processes within groups and between them, connecting personal experience with patterns of belonging, polarization and conflict.

Related projects
Segregation, prejudice and intergroup relations

Our research examines friendship segregation and prejudice, with particular attention to schools and adolescent peer relationships.

Related publications
Social networks

Longitudinal network analysis and agent-based modelling help us understand the structures through which attitudes and behaviours spread.

Related projects
